content.content:
- Banshee on 1.21.x = custom skin + full sound set on a vanilla-model mob; **animated custom-model creatures are 26.x first** (BetterModel v3 needs Java 25).
- Generated mods stay on `plugin.yml` (Paper's `paper-plugin.yml` is still experimental).
- Gameplay Designers, full creature pipeline and worldgen come after the foundation, assets and composition (they are mini-languages each).

## 2b. Built to stand alone later (owner decision, 2026-10-10)
Cyrus stays a part of Nxeon for at least the next few months (to build a solid foundation and gather months of real Nxeon-customer usage data), then may become its own product. So:
- **Nothing breaks and nothing changes for customers:** same sign-in, same accounts, same wallet, same billing. No separate Cyrus login now.
- **Design for the split from day one (cheap now, expensive later):** Cyrus code reaches Nxeon only through a small **host seam** (sign-in/user, plan and billing, server access for install, storage, notifications). New code must not add new direct imports of Nxeon internals; where one is unavoidable it goes behind a named adapter. Cyrus tables stay Cyrus-prefixed with opaque ids for users/servers (no new foreign keys into Nxeon tables). The build service already stands alone; the engine core, asset pipelines, Test Flight and pack hosting already live under `lib/cyrus/` and stay game- and host-agnostic.
- **Later, when separating:** Nxeon implements the host side as an API (list servers, push plugin/pack/config, restart); a standalone Cyrus gets its own sign-in, wallet and billing, own database, and a standalone export (jar and pack download). The Kodely-to-Nxeon partner API is the existing pattern.
- **Not now:** no code that exists only to prepare the split beyond the seam rule and a coupling map.

## 3. Reality check on the facts (from the research)
- Cyrus builds only 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11 on JDK 21. Compile is plain `javac --release 21 -proc:none` against a Paper-only classpath (Gradle only builds classpath files). 4 of 6 explicitly versioned Paper servers on Nxeon already run 26.x, so version support is a top lever. 26.x needs Java 25. **Correction (checked on Paper's Fill API and Maven, 2026-10-10):** stable builds exist only for 26.1.2 (build 74) and 26.2 (build 133); 26.3 has only alpha/beta builds, so the version research was wrong that 26.3 is stable. The 26.x lane starts with **26.2**, then 26.1.2; 26.3 stays preview and unpinned until Paper ships a stable build. The registry now holds the exact pins and server-jar hashes.
- No ModSpec, project/revision store, asset manifest or import flow exist. A "project" is a chain of `ModBuild` rows. `textures/` does item textures only; `sfx.ts` is interface sounds only. The Mods installer treats resource packs as unsupported. `packFormatFor` is wrong for 26.x (returns 75; 26.1 is 76-84). Plan tiers gate models only; the single gate is `gateBuild` at `create.ts:72`, bypassed when tokens are off.
- `server.properties` holds one resource pack; Paper's `Player#addResourcePack(UUID, ...)` allows several and `setResourcePack` is deprecated.
- A vanilla client with a server-pushed pack plus datapack can show items, weapons, armor, food, display-entity mobs, glyph HUDs, GUIs, enchantments, recipes, advancements, bosses, abilities, commands, sounds, biomes and structures. Client-mod-only: brand-new block types, native entity models, free-form HUD widgets, custom keybinds, custom sky.
- Build service auth: it can run on a subscription login. Before ANY public launch, switch to an API key and re-measure cost (not blocking development now).
- Jars are not reproducible today (`jar --create` without `--date`).

## 4. Engine design
### 4.1 Mod project model + revisions (size L)
Typed project: `ModSpec`/content IR (items, mobs, abilities, GUIs, quests, recipes, loot, biomes...), code files, assets, datapacks, config, dependencies, tests, requirement IDs. Stored as immutable revisions with diffs; each revision traces to exact inputs and toolchain; the last passing revision is always preserved. `schemaVersion` with explicit migrations; JSON Schema as the portable contract, Zod types in code. New tables (project, revision, asset, namespace) need an owner-approved DB migration deploy. Chat history is not the project.

### 4.2 Registries and reserved namespaces (S-M)
Capability registry, **version registry**, **identifier registry**, asset registry with provenance. Each project reserves a namespace `nx_<hash>` at creation so IDs, keys, permissions, sound keys, glyph ranges and model paths are collision-free by construction. Version registry holds exact pack format per version (one `pack.mcmeta` style per version family), JDK, classpath hash, capability flags (item model definitions from 1.21.4; Dialog API 1.21.7+; Folia support), status (`preview/supported/deprecated/blocked`). Contract-tested against Paper's Fill API.

### 4.3 Capability router + task spec (M)
After the prompt check: classify what the request needs (plugin / plugin + resource pack / datapack / future client mod), disclose limits, show an editable plan and acceptance criteria before tokens are spent. One schema: this is the Master Plan's `CyrusTaskSpec`, the Roadmap's Mod Specification and the asset manifest. Tier gate is applied here and again inside the build service request.

### 4.4 Generators, build and reproducibility (M)
Deterministic generators emit code/data/packs for common mechanics from the IR; free-form AI code is the fallback. Build: `javac` per version lane (JDK 21 and JDK 25 side by side, per-version `--release`, classpath files fetched by checksum, exact stable pin), scan, package. Make jars byte-stable (`jar --date`, sorted inputs); record **engine release id** (prompt version + sheets + rules + scanner hash + image digest), source/classpath/output hashes, scan report and SBOM per artifact. Rename CYR-004 to "immutable javac/classpath/template".

### 4.5 Managed plugins, Pack Loader, pack hosting (M)
- **ManagedPlugin** records: pinned version per Minecraft family, installed on first dependent mod, ref-counted, not user-removable while depended on. Hosts the Pack Loader and BetterModel.
- **Nxeon Pack Loader**: sends N packs by UUID with `addResourcePack`, per-pack required/optional, accept-rate telemetry, Geyser/Floodgate detection. `server.properties` only as fallback. Conflict engine detects an existing pack owner (ResourcePackManager, Oraxen, Nexo).
- **Pack hosting**: object storage on an Nxeon domain (provider not named to customers), content-addressed immutable URLs `/p/<sha1>.zip`, size caps, retention GC; keep it off the primary node.

Since lib/cyrus shouldn't import from Nxeon, I'm designing a separate service token mechanism distinct from the existing user-facing ApiToken scopes system. Actually, Ed25519 asymmetric signing is a better fit than HMAC: Nxeon signs assertions with a private key while Cyrus only holds the public key to verify them, so leaking Cyrus's config can't let anyone forge assertions, and Node's crypto module supports ed25519 natively. Service tokens stay hashed with sha256.

For where config lives, I'm planning a dedicated `apiV1Config(env)` function in lib/cyrus/api/v1/config.ts that reads straight from process.env rather than piping through the existing cyrusConfig, since the test suite forbids hardcoded path literals — this should satisfy that constraint while keeping the naming consistent with other CYRUS_API_V1_* flags.

I'm settling on a `CYRUS_API_V1` env flag (default off) checked per request, with a strict fail-closed policy: flag off returns 404 as if the endpoint doesn't exist, while flag on but misconfigured keys should return 503 with an `api_misconfigured` error rather than ever silently opening up, and unauthenticated requests when keys are missing should 401.

For the subject assertion, I'm designing a `Cyrus-Subject` header carrying a base64url-encoded payload and signature, where the payload includes version, issuer (client ID), subject ID, audience, issued-at/expiry (capped at 120s) and a jti for replay protection — verification checks issuer matches the client, audience, a 30-second skew window, and a replay cache keyed by jti (in-memory LRU for now, with a note that multi-instance deployments will need shared storage).

I'm also mapping Cyrus subjects to userIds: today within Nxeon, the Nxeon user id doubles as the Cyrus userId, so for this slice I'll just treat sub as userId when issuer is "nxeon," while noting that a standalone CyrusSubject mapping table is planned later. I'm laying out the scope list (health, projects:read, builds:read, catalog:read now, with write/admin scopes reserved for later), and settling on rate limiting per API key via an in-process fixed window with standard RateLimit headers, keeping it simple rather than also limiting per subject. I'm starting to define the error response shape with code, message, and issue fields.

For file operations, I'm sketching a session-based filesystem bridge: opening a remote file session returns a session ID, individual operations hit that session's endpoint, and closing deletes it, with binary data base64-encoded in the JSON body for now as a skeleton approach before streaming is added later.

# Cyrus API v1: inventory and design (r25, 2026-10-10)
Branch `feature/cyrus-r25-api` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`). Direction B of CYRUS-TRACKER section 1: **Nxeon (or any site) calls Cyrus**. Direction A (Cyrus calls Nxeon) is the host seam `lib/cyrus/host`; this API is its mirror image. Nothing here is deployed; everything sits behind `CYRUS_API_V1` (off).

## 1. Inventory: 57 route files today, classified
U = internal UI backend (stays with the Cyrus UI, not public), P = public API candidate, A = admin-only, S = special.

| Group (files) | Today | Class | v1 resource |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mod-builder/builds` GET/POST, `builds/[id]` GET, `cancel`, `jar`, `source`, `source-zip`, `attachments/[n]` (8) | session, owner check | P | `builds` (create, get, cancel, artifacts) |
| `mod-builder/builds/[id]/live` (NDJSON proxy), `cyrus/generate` (forge stream) (2) | session | U now, P later as `events` (SSE) | `builds/{id}/events` |
| `mod-builder/builds/[id]/install` (1) | session, SSH push | P (write, later) | `installs` |
| `mod-builder/projects/[id]` PATCH, `mod-builder/uploads` (2) | session | P | `projects` meta, `uploads` |
| `cyrus/assets/v1/projects` GET, `.../pack` GET (2) | studio viewer | P | `projects/{id}/assets`, `projects/{id}/pack` |
| `cyrus/assets/v1/.../textures/*`, `.../sounds/*` candidates, reject, render, revisions (10) | studio viewer + plan gate | U (studio editing loop) | later `projects/{id}/assets/{slot}/revisions` |
| `cyrus/assets/v1/library` GET, `asset/[id]/png`, `upload`, `use` (4) | viewer + plan | P (read now, write later) | `library`, `catalog` |
| `cyrus/assets/v1/quality`, `sound/preview` (2) | viewer | U | none |
| `cyrus/assets/v1/model-editor/**` (4), `cyrus/models/v1/**` (4) | viewer + plan | U (studio), P later for drafts | `projects/{id}/drafts` |
| `cyrus/import` GET/POST, `[id]` GET/DELETE, `[id]/conflicts` (3) | flag + session | P (write, later) | `imports` |
| `cyrus/tokens` GET, `tokens/plan` POST (2) | session | P (read now via plan), write = owner decision | `account/plan`, `account/tokens` |
| `cyrus/tokens/checkout`, `checkout-line`, `return` (3) | session + Stripe | S: payment flow, stays with the payment owner | none in v1 |
| `cyrus/universe` (1) | preview gate | U (static shape) | `games` (static, later) |
| `nxlabs/cyrus/[slug]/{diff,download,source,media}`, `media/[id]` (5) | public pages / creator | P (read), U (media upload) | `mods` (published listings) |
| `admin/cyrus/ops` (1) | admin role + preview | A | `admin/*` (separate scope, later) |
| `cyrus/ai-gateway/v1/chat` (1) | per-server HMAC token | S: mods call it from game servers; its own contract | none |
| `p/[file]` (1) | public, content-addressed | S: pack hosting, never authenticated | none |
| `stripe/webhook` (Cyrus branch) (1) | Stripe signature | S: Nxeon-owned, becomes a Cyrus webhook consumer | none |

25 pages under `app/**/cyrus*` are UI and are not part of the API. The existing `/api/cyrus/assets/v1` and `/api/cyrus/models/v1` "v1" are UI versions (cookie session); the public API is a new, separate tree **`/api/cyrus/v1/`** so the two never mix.

## 2. Resource model
All ids are opaque strings. Users appear only as a **subject** (see auth).
- **projects**: `CyrusProject` (id `cp…`, game, namespace, title, head/lastPassing revision, revisionCount). `revisions` nested, append-only (seq, kind, status, manifest, ModSpec). Writes later: create, add revision, revert (expectedHeadId = optimistic concurrency, already in engine-core).
- **builds**: `ModBuild` (status queued…succeeded/failed, target version, plugin name/version, jar sha256/size, error code, engine release record, timings). Writes later: create (idempotency key required), cancel. Artifacts: `builds/{id}/jar`, `/source` as short-lived signed download URLs, never raw paths.
- **mods**: published listings (`CyrusModPage`, slug, versions, licence); read-only public data.
- **installs**: request "put build X / mod pack Y on server Z" and its result (async, webhook `install.result`). Cyrus never holds server credentials: the install itself runs through direction A.
- **assets / library**: project asset slots (`CyrusProjectAsset`), user library items, uploads.
- **catalog**: `CatalogEntry` v1 search/get, same gates as the model-facing `catalog_search`/`catalog_get` (plan tier, licence tier, proprietary clearance, published only).
- **account**: plan tier + token balance (read), plan changes (decision below).
- **drafts**: Model Studio / editor drafts (`CyrusModelDraft`), studios specs (MotionSpec, designer specs) as typed documents.
- **events**: build progress (SSE later) and outbound webhooks.
Schemas come from the existing Zod sources (`ModSpecV1Schema`, `CatalogEntrySchema`, `MotionSpecSchema`) through `z.toJSONSchema`; the OpenAPI file is generated, never hand-copied.

## 3. Auth
Two layers, both required for user data:
1. **Service token** (who is calling): `Authorization: Bearer cyk_<keyId>_<secret>`. Cyrus stores only `sha256(secret)` per key with `client`, `scopes[]`, `rpm`. Constant-time compare. Scopes: `health` (implicit), `projects:read`, `builds:read`, `catalog:read`, later `projects:write`, `builds:write`, `installs:write`, `account:read`, `webhooks:manage`, `admin:read`. A missing scope = 403; unknown key = 401; flag off = 404 (route does not exist); bad config = 503; never open.
2. **Subject assertion** (on whose behalf): header `Cyrus-Subject: <b64url(payload)>.<b64url(sig)>`, **Ed25519**-signed by the caller (Nxeon holds the private key, Cyrus only the public key, so a leaked Cyrus config cannot mint identities). Payload `{v:1, iss, sub, aud:"cyrus-api-v1", iat, exp, jti}`; `iss` must equal the token's client; lifetime at most 120 s, 30 s skew; `jti` single-use (replay cache); `sub` is the **stable subject id** (today the Nxeon user id; later an SSO `sub`), **never an email** (a payload carrying `email` is rejected). Every project/build read is owner-checked against `sub`; someone else's object answers 404.
- Browser SSO for a standalone Cyrus site reuses the Kodely pattern (`/sso/authorize` → signed 5-min code → server-side exchange) but fixes its gaps: single-use codes, PKCE, and `sub` as the account link (Kodely links by user id too, good; its codes are replayable inside 5 min).
- **Rotation**: several keys per client may be active (`CYRUS_API_V1_KEYS` is a list); add new, deploy caller, remove old. Subject public keys carry a `kid`; two can be active.
- **Rate limits**: per key (`rpm`, default 120/min), fixed window through `host.rateLimit`; `429` + `Retry-After` + `RateLimit-*` headers. A shared store (Redis/Postgres) replaces the in-process window when Cyrus runs more than one instance.

## 4. Conventions
- **Idempotency**: every POST takes `Idempotency-Key` (required for builds, installs, plan changes). Stored 24 h per (key, client, subject) with the request hash; same key + same body replays the stored response, same key + different body = `409 idempotency_mismatch`. Needs one additive table `CyrusApiIdempotency` (SQL only, later).
- **Pagination**: cursor-based, `?limit=` (1–100, default 20) and `?cursor=` (opaque b64url of the last `createdAt,id`); response `{data:[…], nextCursor:string|null}`. Stable order `createdAt desc, id desc`.
- **Errors**: always `{error:{code, message, issues?:[{path, code, message}], requestId}}`, reusing the engine's `SpecIssue` shape so ModSpec validation errors pass through unchanged. Codes are stable snake_case (`unauthorized`, `forbidden_scope`, `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `bad_request`, `catalog_unavailable`, `api_misconfigured`…).

## 5. Webhooks Cyrus → Nxeon

## 6. Nxeon side and the pairing with direction A

|---|---|---|
| Accounts, sessions, game servers, install records (`ServerMod`/`GameMod`) | Nxeon | Cyrus reads via direction A |
| Projects, revisions, builds, assets, catalog, mod pages, drafts, token ledger | Cyrus | its 28 tables, no FKs into Nxeon |
| Wallet and payments | **owner decision** | Option 1: **Nxeon is the payment provider**: Cyrus asks Nxeon to debit the shared wallet (`billing.debit` with idempotency key), Stripe stays in Nxeon's account, one wallet, no migration of customers. ## 8. Migration path
1. (this branch) design, contract, read-only slice, HTTP adapter skeleton; all off.
2. Nxeon-side partner API for Cyrus (mount `handleHostApi(nxeonHost)`, scoped key) and the Nxeon client; owner-approved idempotency + webhook tables (SQL files).

- Identity: anything keyed by email orphans balances; enforced by the `sub`-only assertion.

- Remote file sessions are chatty (one HTTP call per file op); fine for plugin jars, batch later.
- Replay caches and rate limits are per process in the slice: a multi-instance deploy needs a shared store.
- The catalog index has no production backend yet (r26); the slice reads a configured JSONL file or answers 503.
- Stripe metadata (`cyrusUserId`) and the shared webhook stay Nxeon-side until the wallet decision.

## 10. Owner decisions
1. Wallet: Nxeon as payment provider (recommended) or separate Stripe account.
2. Sign-in at move day: SSO from Nxeon (recommended, one account) or Cyrus's own accounts.
3. API domain (`api.cyrus.<domain>` vs a path on the new site) and whether third parties (beyond Nxeon/Kodely) ever get keys.
4. Who may change plans through the API (Nxeon only, or also Kodely).
5. Retention for webhook dead letters and idempotency records (proposed 24 h / 30 d).

U = internal UI backend (stays with the Cyrus UI, not public), P = public API candidate, A = admin-only, S = special.

| `mod-builder/builds/[id]/install` (1) | session, SSH push | P (write, later) | `installs` |
| `mod-builder/projects/[id]` PATCH, `mod-builder/uploads` (2) | session | P | `projects` meta, `uploads` |
| `cyrus/assets/v1/projects` GET, `.../pack` GET (2) | studio viewer | P | `projects/{id}/assets`, `projects/{id}/pack` |

| `cyrus/assets/v1/library` GET, `asset/[id]/png`, `upload`, `use` (4) | viewer + plan | P (read now, write later) | `library`, `catalog` |
| `cyrus/assets/v1/quality`, `sound/preview` (2) | viewer | U | none |
| `cyrus/assets/v1/model-editor/**` (4), `cyrus/models/v1/**` (4) | viewer + plan | U (studio), P later for drafts | `projects/{id}/drafts` |

| `cyrus/universe` (1) | preview gate | U (static shape) | `games` (static, later) |

All ids are opaque strings. Users appear only as a **subject** (see auth).

- **assets / library**: project asset slots (`CyrusProjectAsset`), user library items, uploads.

content.thinking:
I'm sketching out the config module for API v1, defining a function that reads environment variables to build a config object with API keys, scopes, rate limits, and subject keys, controlled by an enable flag.

Then I'm outlining the other modules: signing.ts handles token hashing, Ed25519 assertion verification, HMAC request/webhook signing, and a replay cache; auth.ts does request authentication returning context or error status; http.ts has framework-free route handlers wired to dependencies like database reads, catalog lookups, and rate limiting; and deps.ts wires up the real dependencies.

I check where the proprietary clearance flag is read, reusing the same fail-closed pattern as CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED so a disabled flag returns a plain 404 not_found rather than exposing route existence. Each request gets a random 12-hex id in a Cyrus-Request-Id header, and I settle on the auth check order: flag check, then config validation, then token auth, then scope check, then rate limiting.

For subject verification, I decide rate limiting happens after token auth per-key since Ed25519 verification is cheap, and I use the same generic 401 message whether the key is unknown or the secret is wrong to avoid leaking info. For project pagination I design a base64url-encoded cursor carrying createdAt and id, with a query that orders by createdAt and id descending and uses a compound inequality to find the next page, validating limit as an integer between 1 and 100 and rejecting bad cursors with a 400 error.

For project retrieval I check ownership against the userId and return 404 if missing or mismatched, then fetch head and last-passing revisions, returning the spec as already-validated stored JSON and counting files from the manifest array length. I want the server to track sessions mapping to filesystem handles with expiry, and support install and close operations that resolve filesystem context from the session. I decide to keep this reference server generic and host-agnostic, living in a shared library path so it can later be mounted with a specific host implementation and tested against a fake in-memory host over real HTTP. I'm covering the remaining methods: settings mutation invalidates the cache, rate limiting uses a local fixed window, worker and user operations map to POST/GET as appropriate, and jobs/servers queries revive dates through a codec. For servers.familyOf I'm relying on a family field the server attaches to rows, falling back to an OS template's family, and for pinnedVersion I'm duplicating the pure rule locally since it can't be imported, noting this mirrors logic elsewhere that a contract test should verify against.

I'm also handling servers.openFiles as a POST returning a session wrapped in a RemoteGuestFs with a close hook, records as simple GETs, and installs.statePath as a getter that fails closed if the snapshot hasn't warmed yet. For installs.install I need to validate the fs comes from this host via a WeakMap session lookup, encode prefetched buffers as base64, and attach an idempotency key that's randomized per call but reused on retries -- the same idempotency pattern applies to audit.record/append. Finally I'm confirming that importing the signing helper from the v1 API module into the host http file stays within the lib/cyrus boundary, so it's fine.

Retries only apply to GETs or idempotency-keyed calls hitting network errors, timeouts, or 429/502/503/504, using exponential backoff with jitter and respecting Retry-After up to five seconds, with each retried attempt re-signed with a fresh nonce and timestamp. The server verifies the signature over method, path-with-query, and body, then dispatches by name through a lookup table mapping method names to handler functions, with fs.* methods needing a session lookup first. ## Cyrus API v1 (2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r25-api`, NOT deployed, behind `CYRUS_API_V1` (off))

Direction B of the Cyrus separation: the external, versioned, token-authenticated API through which Nxeon (or another trusted site) uses Cyrus once Cyrus runs as its own app. Design and route inventory: `docs/api/CYRUS-API-PLAN.md` (copy of `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v6-api/CYRUS-API-PLAN.md`). Direction A (Cyrus calls Nxeon) is the host seam; its HTTP form is below.

**Contract.** `docs/api/cyrus-v1.openapi.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1) is GENERATED by `npx tsx tools/cyrus-api/gen-openapi.ts` from `lib/cyrus/api/v1/schemas.ts` (Zod; reuses `ModSpecV1Schema`, `CatalogEntryV1Z`, `MotionSpecSchema`) and the operation table in `lib/cyrus/api/v1/openapi.ts`. 21 operations (6 `x-cyrus-status: live`, 15 `planned`) and 5 webhooks (`build.finished`, `mod.published`, `install.result`, `delivery.rolledback`, `library.contributed`, all planned). The YAML writer/reader is in-repo (`lib/cyrus/api/v1/yaml.ts`, every string JSON-quoted so any YAML parser reads it). `test/cyrus-api-contract.test.ts` fails when the file drifts from the sources, when it is not valid OpenAPI 3.1 structurally (refs, path params, unique ids, scopes), when a live operation has no handler, when a planned one has one, or when a handler is undocumented. After changing anything in `lib/cyrus/api/v1`, regenerate the file.

**Live endpoints (read-only)** under `/api/cyrus/v1/`: `GET health`, `GET projects`, `GET projects/{projectId}`, `GET builds/{buildId}`, `GET catalog/search`, `GET catalog/entries/{entryId}`. Route files are one-line wrappers; logic in `lib/cyrus/api/v1/http.ts` (framework-free, fakes in tests), real wiring in `deps.ts` (cyrusDb, host rate limiter, tokens `tierOf`).
- Order per request: flag (off = 404) -> config sane (bad JSON/key = 503 `api_misconfigured`, never open) -> service token (401) -> scopes (403 `forbidden_scope`) -> per-key rate limit (429 + `Retry-After`, `RateLimit-*` headers) -> subject assertion for per-user operations (400 `subject_required` / 401 `bad_subject`) -> handler. Someone else's project/build = 404. Errors are always `{error:{code, message, issues?:[{path,code,message}], requestId}}`; a 500 never carries internals.
- **Service tokens**: `Authorization: Bearer cyk_<keyId>_<secret>`. `CYRUS_API_V1_KEYS` holds only `sha256(secret)` per key with `client`, `scopes`, `rpm` (default 120/min); several keys per client = rotation. Scopes: `projects:read`, `builds:read`, `catalog:read` live; `*:write`, `installs:*`, `mods:read`, `account:read`, `webhooks:manage`, `admin:read` reserved. `mintServiceToken()` in `signing.ts` makes a token + hash.
- **Subject assertion**: header `Cyrus-Subject` = `b64url(JSON {v:1, iss, sub, aud:"cyrus-api-v1", iat, exp, jti, kid?})` + `.` + `b64url(Ed25519 signature)`. The caller (Nxeon) holds the private key; `CYRUS_API_V1_SUBJECT_KEYS` holds public keys (base64 DER SPKI) per client + `kid`. `iss` must be the token's client, lifetime at most 120 s (30 s skew), `jti` single use (in-process replay cache), `sub` is the stable subject id (today the Nxeon user id); a payload with an `email` field or an `@` in `sub` is refused.
- **Pagination**: `limit` + opaque `cursor` -> `{data, nextCursor}` (projects: `createdAt desc, id desc`; catalog: offset cursor).
- **Catalog**: same gates as the model-facing `catalog_search`/`catalog_get` (plan kinds and licence tiers from `tierOf`, proprietary library only with `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`, published only; a gated entry is a 404). Public fields only (no provenance paths). Backend: `CYRUS_API_V1_CATALOG_FILE` (CatalogEntry JSONL, max 64 MB, memory index) until the catalog's database index lands; unset = 503 `catalog_unavailable`.
- Builds: public view only (no cost, jar path, raw result); reads the row, never polls the build service.

**HTTP host adapter (direction A skeleton).** `lib/cyrus/host/http.ts` `createHttpHost({baseUrl, keyId, secret, db, session})` implements `CyrusHost` over fetch: every call HMAC-signed (`cyrus-key-id`, `cyrus-timestamp`, `cyrus-nonce`, `cyrus-signature: v1=hex(HMAC(method, path+query, ts, nonce, sha256(body)))`), timeout per attempt (8 s), 2 retries with backoff for reads and for writes (writes carry one `Idempotency-Key` across retries). Local by design: `db`, `rateLimit`, `access.canAccess`, `servers.familyOf/pinnedVersion`, `installs.statePath` (from `warm()` = `host.info`; before it `canAccess` is false and `statePath` throws). Remote files are a file session (`servers.openFiles` -> `fs.*` -> `fs.close`), and installs go through that session, so server credentials never leave the platform. Protocol table: `lib/cyrus/host/http-protocol.ts` (`HOST_API_PREFIX = /api/partner/cyrus/host/v1`, 46 calls, Buffer/Date codec). Reference server: `lib/cyrus/host/http-server.ts` `createHostServer(anyHost, {secretFor, roleAreas, roleOf})` (signature + replay + idempotency replay + key-bound sessions; role always from the platform). # V - Cyrus API v1 (r25, 2026-10-10)
Branch `feature/cyrus-r25-api` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r25`, from `feature/cyrus-r2` @ 9afe84d58e). NOT merged, NOT deployed, flag `CYRUS_API_V1` OFF. No migration, no table, no Nxeon behaviour change (new files only, plus a docs section).

## Commits
1. `a31e54f088` design + inventory: `docs/api/CYRUS-API-PLAN.md` (= `cyrus-designs/v6-api/CYRUS-API-PLAN.md`). 57 route files classified (P public candidate / U UI-only / A admin / S special), resource model, auth, idempotency, pagination, errors, versioning, webhooks, data ownership (both wallet options), migration path, risks, owner decisions.
2. `a46850f1de` contract: `docs/api/cyrus-v1.openapi.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1) generated from Zod (`lib/cyrus/api/v1/schemas.ts` reuses ModSpecV1Schema, CatalogEntryV1Z, MotionSpecSchema) + operation table `openapi.ts`; generator `tools/cyrus-api/gen-openapi.ts`; `test/cyrus-api-contract.test.ts`.
3. `252b9f64c1` read-only slice under `app/api/cyrus/v1/`: health, projects list/get, builds get, catalog search/get.
4. `10611085f3` HTTP host adapter skeleton: `lib/cyrus/host/http.ts`, `http-protocol.ts`, `http-server.ts`, `test/cyrus-host-http.test.ts`.
5. docs (this commit): DOCUMENTATION.md "Cyrus API v1", OWNER-ACTIONS section, tracker 1B status, this report.

## Design choices worth knowing
- Two auth layers: service token (`cyk_<id>_<secret>`, only sha256 stored, scopes, per-key rpm) plus an **Ed25519-signed subject assertion** (Cyrus holds only the public key, so a leaked Cyrus config cannot mint identities). `sub` is the stable id; email is refused outright. 120 s max lifetime, single-use `jti`.
- Improves on the Kodely pattern it copies: scopes instead of one shared key, replay protection on assertions and webhooks, dedicated webhook secret (as Kodely already does), no AUTH_SECRET reuse.
- Contract is generated, never hand-copied; the test enforces live/planned honesty in both directions.
- Direction A over HTTP keeps `db`, `rateLimit` and the synchronous methods local; guest files are remote file sessions bound to the calling key, and installs run through them, so SSH credentials never leave Nxeon.
- New public tree `/api/cyrus/v1/` is separate from the UI's cookie-session `/api/cyrus/assets/v1` and `/models/v1`.

## Ran (all on node-2 via devhost)
- Full Cyrus suite `test/cyrus-*.test.ts`: **1906/1906 pass**, 0 skipped (includes the PyYAML cross-check of the contract file).
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean (after commit 4).
- New tests: contract 29, slice 26, HTTP host 13. The HTTP host conformance suite runs identically on a fake host and on `createHttpHost` over a real local HTTP server (Buffers, Dates, file sessions, install with prefetched bytes, settings, audit).
- **One real HTTP run**: `devhost db push`, `tools/cyrus-api/dev-seed.ts` (refuses non-`wt_*` DBs), `next dev` on node-2 with throwaway keys, tunnel + curl: health 200; projects 200; project 200 (head, lastPassing, spec); build 200 (no cost/jarPath); other subject's build 404; catalog search 200 and entry 200 on a 300-entry sample of the staged catalog; model search on Saka 403 `asset_locked`; no token 401; replayed assertion 401. Dev server stopped, tunnel closed, sample file deleted. The throwaway DB `wt_cyrus_r25` and its devhost env (test key hash, test public key) remain; `devhost rm` clears them.

## Not run / not built
- No write endpoints (builds, installs, revisions, plan changes), no idempotency table, no webhook sender or Nxeon receiver, no Nxeon-side client or assertion minting, no SSE events, no signed artifact URLs.
- The host reference server is mounted nowhere; no real Nxeon endpoint was called. `auth.user` role defaults to USER unless the platform passes `roleOf`.
- Replay caches and rate limits are in-process (one instance only).
- Catalog backend is a JSONL memory index (max 64 MB) until r26's database index; the staged files (120 MB) are over that cap on purpose.
- No load test; no next build of the app (tsc only).
- Merge risk: the contract test pins `docs/api/cyrus-v1.openapi.yaml`; anyone changing ModSpec/CatalogEntry/MotionSpec Zod must regenerate it (`npx tsx tools/cyrus-api/gen-openapi.ts`), or the test fails. That is intended.

## Owner decisions (also in OWNER-ACTIONS.md)
Wallet (Nxeon as payment provider, recommended, vs own Stripe); SSO from Nxeon (recommended) vs own accounts; API domain and third-party keys; who may change plans/start builds via API; retention for idempotency and dead letters; later approve the idempotency + webhook tables (SQL only).
